service.name: Corporate retreat entertainment
service.serviceType: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events
service.description: Live music for corporate retreats and incentive events in the Colorado mountain corridor, solo through quartet, with travel and lodging itemised as their own lines.

faqs.q: What does live music cost at a mountain resort?
faqs.a: A resort date costs more than a metro date for two reasons, both named on the quote as their own lines. Travel, because Vail and Beaver Creek are a mountain highway from Denver and Aspen is most of a working day each way. And a night's lodging past the passes, because a band that struck at eleven is not driving back at one in the morning. A five to six piece band in Mountain West markets runs {{market:mountain_west_band}}, which is the market to budget against.

faqs.q: What does the resort need to provide?
faqs.a: One or two dedicated 20-amp circuits within reach of the performance area, a load-in window of 45 to 90 minutes depending on size, and the cap and curfew figures at contract. Dedicated is the word that matters: sharing a circuit with catering warmers is the most common cause of a load-in problem.

faqs.q: Do you honour decibel caps and curfews?
faqs.a: Yes, as written. Mountain venues run on their own rules, so tell us the cap and the curfew when you book and both go into the plan, including how the last twenty minutes are shaped to land on the curfew.

faqs.q: Can the band play outdoors at altitude?
faqs.a: Yes, on a covered, level and dry performance area with power run to it and a move-indoors call time written before the day. Mountain evenings drop fast, and instruments and electronics both stop behaving in the cold. Altitude also changes pacing: singers and horn players tire faster in thin air, so the night is paced for it.

No. Lodging applies on far-resort dates, Aspen among them, and is billed at cost as its own line on the quote, the receipt and nothing added. It exists because far-resort dates are two-day commitments for the band, whatever the run of show says.
